title: sqlc-pgx-monitoring
description: Traces, metrics and logs emitted by dbtracer and poolstatus.

panels.title: Overview — is the database layer serving, failing or slow?
Operations/s
panels.description: Every traced pgx operation (query, prepare, batch, copy_from, connect) per second. Normal: steady with the workload. Action: a drop to 0 means the app stopped talking to Postgres or stopped exporting.

panels.title: Failed share
panels.description: Share of operations whose pgx.status is not OK. The example workload fails on purpose (unique violation, failed batch, wrong password), so a few percent is normal here. Action: find the query in Queries → Failures.

panels.title: Query p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of postgresql.query duration across all queries. Normal: under 100ms for the example workload (raw-sql sleeps up to 100ms). Action: find the slow query in Queries → Latency.

panels.title: Connections in use
panels.description: Connections checked out of the pool now (db.client.connections.usage, state=used). Normal: below the pool max. Action: at max with acquire waits rising, the pool is too small or queries hold connections too long.

panels.title: Acquire p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of time spent in pgxpool Acquire (pgx.pool.trace.acquire.duration). Normal: well under 1ms when idle connections exist. Action: rising with pool pressure means callers queue for connections.

panels.title: Canceled acquires
panels.description: Acquires abandoned because the caller's context ended while waiting, over the dashboard range. The example cancels one acquire every 10 rounds. Action: in production any increase means callers time out waiting for the pool.

panels.title: Queries — which sqlc queries are hot, slow or failing?
Rate by query
panels.description: Operations per second per sqlc query name and pgx operation. Raw SQL without a sqlc header is left out. Normal: each query follows its caller's traffic.

panels.title: Latency p95 by query
panels.description: 95th percentile duration per sqlc query (query, prepare and batch operations). Normal: flat lines. Action: a line climbing alone is that query's plan or data; all climbing is the database.

panels.title: Failures by query and status
panels.description: Failed operations per second by sqlc query and pgx.status (the PostgreSQL severity, or UNKNOWN_ERROR for driver errors). The workload's CreateUser and InsertUsers fail with SQLSTATE 23505 by design. Action: open Traces → Failed operations for the SQLSTATE.

panels.title: Query summary
panels.description: One row per sqlc query and operation over the last 5 minutes: rate, latency percentiles and failure share. Sort by a column to find the hottest, slowest or most failing query.

targets.expr: (sum by (sqlc_query_name, pgx_operation_type) (rate(db_client_operation_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",db_namespace=~"$db",sqlc_query_name=~"$query",sqlc_query_name!="",pgx_status!="OK"}[5m])) or (0 * sum by (sqlc_query_name, pgx_operation_type) (rate(db_client_operation_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",db_namespace=~"$db",sqlc_query_name=~"$query",sqlc_query_name!=""}[5m])))) / sum by (sqlc_query_name, pgx_operation_type) (rate(db_client_operation_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",db_namespace=~"$db",sqlc_query_name=~"$query",sqlc_query_name!=""}[5m]))

panels.title: Operations — how each pgx operation type behaves
Rate by operation
panels.description: Operations per second by pgx.operation.type. prepare follows new statements on new connections; connect follows pool churn. Normal: query dominates.

panels.title: Latency p95 by operation
panels.description: 95th percentile duration by pgx.operation.type, raw SQL included. Normal: connect is the slowest (TCP, auth); query and batch track the workload.

panels.title: Query latency distribution
panels.description: postgresql.query operations per latency bucket. Two bands are two code paths; a band drifting up is the population slowing. The example's raw-sql sleeps spread 0–100ms.

panels.title: Pool — is the pool sized right?
Connections
panels.description: Pool connections by state with the configured max (poolstatus). Normal: used well below max, idle above zero. Action: used pinned at max means acquires queue.

panels.title: Acquire and release
panels.description: Connections acquired and released per second, from the tracer hooks (pgx.pool.trace.*) and from pool statistics (pgx.pool.acquires). Normal: all three overlap; acquires above releases means connections leak.

panels.title: Acquire latency
panels.description: Time to acquire a connection: percentiles from the tracer histogram and the mean from pool statistics. Normal: microseconds. Action: p99 jumping with waited acquires means the pool is exhausted.

panels.title: Waited and canceled acquires
panels.description: Acquires per interval that found the pool empty and waited, and those the caller gave up on. The example forces both: pool-pressure every 15 rounds, canceled-acquire every 10. Action: sustained waits mean raise MaxConns or shorten queries.

panels.title: Mean wait when the pool is empty
panels.description: Mean time an acquire waited for a connection to be released or created, from pgx.pool.acquire.wait.duration / pgx.pool.waited_for_acquires. Normal: no line between pressure bursts.

panels.title: Connections created and destroyed
panels.description: Connections opened and closed per interval, closures split by reason (lifetime: MaxConnLifetime, idletime: MaxConnIdleTime). The example uses a 1m lifetime and 20s idle time, so churn is constant.

panels.title: Failed spans
panels.description: Spans from dbtracer with error status: SQLSTATE in db.response.status_code, the error as an exception event. Click a trace to open it in Tempo.

panels.title: Batches
panels.description: Batch traces: one postgresql.batch span with a postgresql.batch.query child per queued query; expand a row for its spans. A failed batch still ends every child; children pgx never reported carry the batch error.

panels.title: Slow queries
panels.description: postgresql.query spans slower than 50ms. With WithIncludeSQLText the statement is in db.query.text.

panels.title: Pool acquires and connects
panels.description: pgxpool.acquire and postgresql.connect spans. A connect nested in an acquire is the pool creating a connection on demand.

panels.title: Error logs
panels.description: Tracer log records at error level, exported through the otelslog bridge. trace_id links each record to its span.

targets.expr: {service_name="$service"} | detected_level="error" | line_format "{{ __line__ }}{{ with .query_name }} {{ . }}{{ end }}{{ with .statement_name }} {{ . }}{{ end }}{{ with .tableName }} {{ . }}{{ end }}{{ with .error }}: {{ . }}{{ end }}"

panels.title: All logs
panels.description: Every tracer log record. The default ShouldLog logs each operation at info; WithShouldLog narrows it.

targets.expr: {service_name="$service"} | line_format "{{ __line__ }}{{ with .query_name }} {{ . }}{{ end }}{{ with .statement_name }} {{ . }}{{ end }}{{ with .tableName }} {{ . }}{{ end }}{{ with .error }}: {{ . }}{{ end }}"
